headline: High: shared project-directory writes plus unrestricted shell/network in gpt-engineer create dangerous default conflict and cascading-error paths with Argo Workflows outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows can emit artifacts/parameters that gpt-engineer reads from the project directory, so attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary. There is no documented provenance tracking or isolation in gpt-engineer, and Argo’s API-driven outputs can be treated as trusted input. This is not proven via sandboxing, so uncertainty stays medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Argo-produced artifacts are copied into gpt-engineer's project directory
IF gpt-engineer parses file contents as instructions or prompts
mitigations: Keep Argo outputs in a separate read-only directory
Add a manual review step before copying artifacts into gpt-engineer
Prefix imported files with provenance headers
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files
requires-engineering: add content provenance and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo touches artifacts and parameters, while gpt-engineer reads and writes the user-specified project directory and can execute code with the user's privileges. If sensitive artifacts are placed in that shared workspace, gpt-engineer can expose them through its broad network egress or model calls. The pair lacks documented isolation, so the shared-workspace leakage path is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF sensitive artifacts or parameters are stored in the shared project directory
IF gpt-engineer sends file contents to its configured model backend or executes code that exfiltrates data
mitigations: Store sensitive artifacts outside the project directory
Use a redacted copy of inputs for gpt-engineer
Restrict outbound network during runs
Review generated code before execution
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data-loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo can write workflow artifacts while gpt-engineer has write_filesystem=true and session_scope is per-project with shared_state via the project directory. That creates overlapping mutable access to the same directory without any locking or coordination primitive in either profile. Because both can modify the same workspace, race conditions and overwrite conflicts are dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory
IF Argo writes artifacts while gpt-engineer writes generated files in the same path
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Serialize access with a manual handoff
Use immutable artifact snapshots
Check in changes only after diff review
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transactional workspace coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo outputs artifacts and parameters that gpt-engineer can consume as project inputs, and gpt-engineer’s tool-use pattern writes files then offers to run them. That makes A’s outputs a likely authority source for B, with no documented verification step. If Argo emits a bad artifact, gpt-engineer can propagate it into code or execution, causing downstream failures or unsafe actions.
conditions: IF gpt-engineer uses Argo-generated artifacts as authoritative inputs
IF generated code is executed after file writes without independent validation
mitigations: Require human review of Argo outputs before use
Validate artifacts against schemas
Run generated code in a disposable sandbox
Compare outputs against expected checksums
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Argo is an open-source workflow engine with no stated residency or retention constraints, while gpt-engineer handles OPENAI_API_KEY and sends prompts to a configured model backend. If regulated data is placed into the shared project directory, the pair can create retention and processing-policy mismatches. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction breach, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared project directory
IF the configured model backend retains prompts or artifacts beyond the operator's policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Use a local or contractually approved model backend
Minimize secrets in prompts and files
Document retention expectations before runs
requires-engineering: implement policy-aware data routing and retention controls
